concepts.why: The patient presented with acute, severe precordial chest pain radiating to the left arm, accompanied by sweating and nausea, and had elevated serum troponin I level, indicating myocardial damage.

The patient experienced similar chest pain at rest that resolved spontaneously after 30 minutes, and had 95% stenosis of the proximal left anterior descending artery, indicating unstable coronary artery disease.
The patient had a history of hypertension for 5 years, treated with reserpine, and presented with elevated blood pressure, indicating potential hypertensive heart disease.
The patient had 95% stenosis of the proximal left anterior descending artery and hypomotility in the anterior wall, indicating coronary artery disease.
The patient presented with acute, severe precordial chest pain and had elevated serum troponin I level, but without ST-segment elevation, indicating non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction.
The patient presented with acute, severe precordial chest pain and had elevated serum troponin I level, with ST-segment elevation in lead avR, indicating ST-elevation myocardial infarction.

rationales.F01: The patient's symptoms of acute, severe precordial chest pain radiating to his left arm, accompanied by sweating and nausea, are highly suggestive of an acute myocardial infarction.
rationales.F02: The patient's history of similar chest pain at rest that resolved spontaneously after 30 minutes is consistent with unstable angina.
rationales.F09: The elevated serum troponin I level is a strong indicator of myocardial infarction.
rationales.F10: The 95% stenosis of the proximal left anterior descending artery is a strong indicator of coronary artery disease and myocardial infarction.

frontier_selector.rationale: Elevated serum troponin I level and ECG changes, including ST-segment elevation, are consistent with acute myocardial infarction, and the presence of 95% stenosis of the proximal left anterior descending artery supports this diagnosis.
